briefing.text: On News, Information Technology stays first (buzz 87.9, down 0.4 on the day, up 0.9 on the week; mentions up 28%; sentiment 0.04), led by NVDA, MSFT and AMD. Financials is the biggest News riser, moving from rank 6 to 2 (buzz 86.6, up 4.8 on the day and 11.0 on the week; mentions up 5%; sentiment 0.03) on BAC, UBS and MS. On X, Information Technology is first again (buzz 93.3, down 0.3; mentions down 5%; sentiment 0.12; NVDA, AMD, CRWV), while the small Technology bucket jumped 8.6 on 250% more mentions but is just one ticker, DRK. On Reddit, Information Technology leads (buzz 95.2, up 1.0; mentions up 123%; sentiment -0.02; NVDA, AMD, AAPL) and Utilities is the weakest (buzz down 6.7 on the day and 8.5 on the week; mentions down 52%; VST, BEP).

NVDA #1: headlines about the chip sector's reaction to Nvidia's pullback and one on 'scenarios after Jensen Huang's resignation'; it is a heavily covered name (2,341 articles in 2 days, 603 negative vs 238 positive), and earnings are due 11-17, so this fits the ranking.
KLAR #2: Klarna hired a Robinhood executive as CFO, and a Yahoo piece on the new CFO's challenges is negative; the stock is up about 8.7%, so the news is thin but fits the move.
KDP #3: only routine trading-volume alerts and an unrelated earnings-call item; it does not explain the rank, which comes from attention and volume.
NU #4: record $1.1 billion quarterly profit and a 7.7% jump in the stock, plus heavy call-option buying; this explains the rise from #11.
GPUCOMPUTE #6: shares Nvidia's attention data; the headlines are Nvidia-related, not about GPU rental prices.
UST30Y #7 / FED #10 / UST10Y #11: the Fed released a revised 2027 calendar with 7 rate decisions, and Treasury reported October spending of $773 billion vs $368.94 billion collected; FOMC is Dec 9.
CRWV #8: earnings-week scorecard says AI-infrastructure names pulled back, and a piece on Nvidia leadership uncertainty weighing on the sector; fits the attention.
TTWO #9: reports of a new GTA VI Online release date lifted the stock; this matches the attention, though the rank fell from #3.

NVDA ranks first (score 0.926) mainly on attention: 2.0 times normal overall (99.5th percentile) and volume 3.1 times normal (top of its range), with an earnings catalyst on 11-17; X attention is about normal at 1.05. KLAR is second (0.903, up from 5): price move is 3.3 sigmas, in the top of its range, with attention about 87th percentile and an earnings catalyst on 11-17. KDP is third (0.900, down from 2): attention is in the 95.5th percentile, volume 1.3 times normal and a Kalshi point-of-sale market trades heavily, but it has no catalyst and its recent news is mostly negative-tilted (26 of 37 articles).

notes: Ranks are by the scoring of record (pick_rank, w2). Prices and moves as of the last pull of the day. Facts from public data; not investment advice.
